text:
Victory to Shri Ramchandra! You are truth, pure awareness, the joy that fills everything — the Supreme Being. You were unseen and without form, and you took a visible form only for the sake of your divine play. When Brahma and all the gods and the perfected sages were breaking down under the cruelty of the demons, you were moved by their helplessness and took a human body, spotless and full of every good quality.
Victory to you! In the home of Dasharath, the blessed king of Kosala, and of the great queen Kaushalya, who was herself a blessing, you appeared as four brothers — like the four beautiful fruits of moksha (salokya, samipya, sarupya and sayujya: living in God's own world, staying near Him, sharing His form, merging into Him). You brought joy to the sacrifices and duties the Vedas teach, to dharma, to the earth, to cows, to brahmins, to devotees and to holy people.
Victory to you! You guarded Vishvamitra's sacrifice (by killing the demons), you crushed the wicked who tormented good people, you washed away the sins of Ahalya, the wife of Gautam, who had been turned to stone by a curse, you broke Shiva's bow and ground down the pride of the whole gathering of kings, and you bowed the head of Parashuram, who held it high with pride in his strength, his courage and his victories.
Victory to you! You are steady and strong in carrying the weight of dharma, and a hero beyond compare in the line of Raghu. Honouring the word of your guru, your mother, your father and your brother, you went to the forests of Chitrakoot, the Vindhyas and Dandak, and by walking in those holy woods you made them blessed and fulfilled.
Victory to Shri Ramchandra! You gave the cheating Jayant, Indra's son, exactly what his deed deserved when he came in the shape of a crow. You dug a pit and buried the demon Viradh in it. You saw through the demoness Shurpanakha, who came in the form of a lovely goddess-maiden, and had her nose and ears cut off — and in this way you turned your face against Ravan, who stood in the way of the whole world's happiness.
Victory to Shri Ramchandra! You are the one who killed Khar, Trishira and Dushan with their army of fourteen thousand, and Marich too. Won over by the love of Jatayu, the flesh-eating vulture, and of Shabari, a woman of low birth, you lifted them both up. You are the ocean of compassion, your life is without a single stain, and you take away the three kinds of suffering.
Victory to Shri Ramchandra! You killed the wicked Kabandh, who was blind with pride; you struck down the mighty Bali and made Sugriv king; you gathered a great army of brave monkeys and bears and drew them up in battle order; and when Vibhishan came to you for shelter you gave him freedom and love for you, and made him rich beyond measure.
Victory to Shri Ramchandra! As easily as play, you built a bridge across the ocean. Lanka, which even the mind of Death could not reach, you seized in one joyful rush. And you destroyed Ravan in battle along with his family, his brothers and his whole army, and set the three worlds free from fear, and Indra, Kuber and the other guardians of the worlds as well.
Victory to Shri Ramchandra! Having won Lanka, you climbed into the flying chariot Pushpak with Lakshman, Janaki, Sugriv, Hanuman and your other ministers, and set out for your own capital, Ayodhya. Tulsidas sings that when you reached there, and Shri Ram became the great king and Sita the great queen, every single person of Ayodhya was filled with the highest joy.

Victory to Shri Ramchandra! Among the kings of kings he is Indra himself. His eyes are as beautiful as lotuses. His name in this age of Kali is a wish-granting tree. He is the one who comforts (those who come to him for shelter) and steadies their hearts. To drink up the ocean of injustice he is the sage Agastya, and to destroy the thick, terrible darkness of the demon hordes he is the blazing sun.
Victory to Shri Ramchandra! Shri Ram, the son of Dasharath, the master of sages, gods and human beings, raised the people of Ayodhya so high that even sages and gods began to bow to them. He is the sun himself — he ends the grief and burning ache of the chakwa birds that are the guardians of the worlds, and he makes the lotus-bed of the Sun dynasty open and bloom.
Victory to Shri Ramchandra! The glow of his body is like a garland of blue lotuses grown in the lake of beauty itself. He is the home of every divine quality, he works for the good of the whole world, and with his form — full of all good fortune, all beauty and the highest splendour — he humbles the pride of millions of Kamadevs, gods of love.
Victory to Shri Ramchandra! He carries the beautiful Sharnga bow, a quiver, arrows, a spear, a shield, a sword and fine armour. He is steady in carrying the weight of dharma, the greatest hero in the line of Raghu; the strength of his mighty arms has no equal; and as if in play he destroyed the demons and lifted the heavy load off the earth.
Victory to Shri Ramchandra! On his head he wears a golden crown set with jewels, and in his ears earrings shaped like fish. On his forehead is the lovely shine of the tilak, and his face glows like the moon. He wears yellow silk, heavenly ornaments and the sacred thread. Who has ever held this form of Shri Ram in his heart, so sweet to the eyes, and not been blessed by it?
Victory to Shri Ramchandra! Bharat, Lakshman and Shatrughna serve him; to Sugriv, Sumant and his other ministers and to his devotees he gives happiness and everything they long for. And the lowly, the hurting, the poor, the fallen and the worst of sinners — if they bow to him even once and say only "protect me", he saves them from this world of birth and death.
Victory to the great king Shri Ramchandra! His pure fame shines through all fourteen worlds; he is holy through and through, and blessed. The Ganga of his story flows down from the Himalaya that is the first poet, the great sage Valmiki; bathing in it and drinking its water — that is, hearing his story and thinking it over — the company of holy people is always happy.
Victory to Shri Ramchandra! In his famous reign, Ram-rajya, every woman and man lived by the conduct laid down for their own station in life; they kept the vows of truth, calm, self-control, kindness and giving; they were free of sorrow and fault, always content, happy in every way, and they always sang and listened to the story of Ram's rule — that is, with nothing left to worry about, they only sang and heard the deeds of Ram.
Victory to Shri Ramchandra! He is the ocean of detachment, of knowledge and of the living experience of it. He gives happiness to those who bow to him and takes away all their sins and all their burning pain. O Lord of Janaki! O destroyer of doubt! This Tulsidas has come to you for shelter — be kind, and give him the support of your feet, which protect everyone who bows there.

O my mind, worship the merciful Shri Ramchandra. He takes away the terrible fear of birth and death in this world; his eyes are like lotuses that have just opened, and his face, his hands and his feet are like red lotuses too.
The splendour of his beauty is greater than that of countless Kamadevs. His body has the lovely colour of a fresh, dark, rain-heavy cloud, and the yellow silk on that cloud-like body flashes like lightning. To that holy and beautiful Shri Ram, the husband of Janaki, I bow.
O my mind, worship Shri Ram, the son of Dasharath — the friend of the poor and helpless, blazing like the sun, the one who tears out the families of demons root and all, the very root of joy, the spotless moon in the sky of the land of Kosala.
On his head is a crown set with jewels, in his ears are earrings, on his forehead a lovely tilak, and on every limb beautiful ornaments shine. His arms reach down to his knees; he holds a bow and arrows; in battle he defeated Khar and Dushan.
He gladdens the heart of Shiva, of Shesh and of the sages, and he destroys our enemies — desire, anger, greed and the rest. Tulsidas prays: may that Raghunath live forever in the lotus of my heart.

O foolish mind! Always, again and again, say only the name of Ram. It is the mine of all good fortune and happiness, and it is the very essence of the Vedas. Understand this in your heart, believe it completely, and keep saying the name of Ram.
The body of Shri Ramchandra, the king of Kosala, glows like a fresh blue lotus; he is the bee who delights in the lotus of the heart of Shiva, who burned Kamadev to ashes. He is the beloved of Janaki, the home of happiness, the one Lord of the whole universe, the destroyer of the wicked in battle, and endlessly kind.
He is like fire to the forest of demons. In his strong arms, long enough to reach his knees, he holds a beautiful bow and fierce arrows. His hands, his feet, his face and his eyes are as lovely as red lotuses. He is the home of every good quality and a treasury holding the beauty of many Kamadevs.
He is the sun itself, closing the night-lilies of our many cravings, and the frost that kills the lotus-bed of desire, anger and pride; he is the lion of the forest for the wild, drunken elephant of greed; and for the good of his devotees he killed the demons and lifted the burden off the world.
His name is Keshav; he destroys all our troubles; Brahma and Shiva bow at his two feet — the feet from which the Ganga was born. He is joy itself gathered together, the destroyer of delusion, and the ship for crossing the terrifying ocean of this world.
Shri Ram is the wind that scatters the gathered clouds of sorrow and doubt, and the thunderbolt that breaks the hard mountain of sin. His name is beyond compare: for holy people it is the wish-granting cow that gives them whatever they long for, it brings peace, and nothing can match it in destroying the heavy sins of the age of Kali.
This name of Ram is a garden of the wish-granting trees of dharma, the food for the road for travellers going to God's own home, and the root support of every practice and every power. Devotion, detachment, deep knowledge, calm, self-control, giving and the many other ways to moksha (freedom) — all of them depend on this name of Ram.
Whoever, seeing this cruel age of Kali, has drunk day and night the flawless nectar of Ram's name — he has done every penance, performed every sacrifice, given away all he owned, and carried out every Vedic rite exactly as it is laid down.
Many outcastes, wrongdoers, Bhils and people of foreign tribes reached the highest home of Hari by the blazing power of Ram's name alone, and no impurity even touched their minds. O Tulsidas! Let go of every hope and every fear, and always say the name of Ram, which is like a sharp sword to cut the chains that bind you to this world.

O my mind! Perform the arati of Shri Ramchandra, the hero of Raghu's line, in this way. He destroys the pairs of opposites, the liking and the hating, and all sorrow; he brings the senses under control and rains down joy.
The whole world, living and lifeless, is the form of Hari; he is everywhere and he is forever — make this thought the incense you burn for him, and its fragrance will drive out the foul smell of seeing differences. After the incense the lamp should be shown, so light the self-shining lamp of knowledge of the Self and let it destroy the darkness of anger, pride and delusion. In this light of knowledge, the proud turnings of your mind will fade away on their own.
After this, offer God the food-offering of pure and noble feeling; a lovely offering of unmixed feeling will please the Lord of Lakshmi more than anything. Then offer him the paan of "love", which destroys sorrow, every doubt, and the very seed of endless worldly craving.
Then take the ten workings of the senses, soaked in the ghee of good and bad deeds, burn them in the fire of letting go, and make the pure light of goodness blaze up; in this way offer the arati of a whole row of lamps — devotion, detachment and true knowledge — to God, who lives in all the worlds.
When the arati is over, in the temple of your clean heart spread out a beautiful bed of peace, lay the great king Shri Ramchandra on it and let him rest. There, to serve the king, appoint forgiveness, compassion and the other chief maidservants. Where Lord Hari stays, the maya that makes us see differences cannot stay.
Sanak and his brothers, the Vedas, Shukdev, Shesh, Shiva, Narad and all the sages who have seen the truth are forever busy with an arati like this; Tulsi, the servant of those pure-minded sages, says that whoever performs such an arati is freed from desire and every other fault and crosses this ocean of the world.

The arati of Shri Ramchandra takes away all the pain of those who suffer. It burns up sorrow and sin, and pulls craving out by the roots and throws it away.
It is sweet-smelling incense and a row of shining lamps. Hearing the sound of hands clapping during the arati, the birds that are our sins fly away at once.
This arati destroys the darkness of ignorance in the house that is the devotee's heart, and spreads a clean light of true understanding.
It is the winter night that closes the lotuses of delusion, pride, anger and the age of Kali; it is the messenger who brings us to meet our beloved, freedom; and the glow of its body is like lightning.
It is a string of moonbeams that makes the night-lilies — the devotees who have come for shelter — open and bloom, and it is like many goddesses Kalika together, to crush the buffalo-demon of Tulsidas's pride.

Hari-Shankari (Hari and Shankar together)
O Vishnu — you are the fire that burns the forest of demons, a forest of virtues yourself, rich in every pure and gentle quality, the master of the senses, the joy of Nand, Upanand and all of them, and you never perish.
O Shiva — you are known by names that bring blessing: Shambhu, Shiva, Rudra, Shankar; you are hugely fearsome, vast in splendour, and anger itself gathered into one.
O Vishnu — you are endless, complete in the six kinds of greatness, the one who brings the world to its end, who wipes away the terror of Yama, the husband of Lakshmi, and the joy of the whole universe.
O Shiva — you are the king of Kailash, the Lord of the world, Ishan, solid knowledge itself, and the home of wisdom and of freedom.
O Vishnu — you took the form of the dwarf Vaman; the mind and the senses cannot reach you; you are pure and untouched by change, the Lord of all that lives and all that does not, the Lord of this world and the next, the Supreme Self himself, the master of nature.
O Shiva — you wear the moon on your head and hold the trident in your hand; you draw creation back into yourself; you are without sin, unborn, beyond all measure, undivided, and you ride on Nandi.
O Vishnu — your body is dark like a blue rain cloud, your beauty is that of many Kamadevs, your eyes are as lovely as lotuses, and you are the kind Lord who lives in everything there is.
O Shiva — your body is smooth, white and fragrant like a conch and like camphor, without a speck of dirt; you wear your matted hair piled on your head and hold the Ganga there, and you wear a garland of white flowers.
O Vishnu — you wear yellow silk the colour of the pollen of a lotus, and in your hands you hold the conch, the disc, the lotus, the Sharnga bow and the huge Kaumodaki mace.
O Shiva — you are the lion that kills the maddened elephant of desire; you have three eyes; you destroy the net of this world of coming and going. To such a Shiva I bow.
O Vishnu — you draw every heart to you, you are the home of compassion, you tamed the serpent Kaliya, and you left Kansa and many other wicked ones with no family to follow them.
O Shiva — you ground down the pride of Tripurasur, you wear the hide of the maddened elephant, and you are the Garuda that swallows the snake that was the demon Andhak.
O Vishnu — you are the complete Brahma, present in everything that moves and everything that does not, without parts, the highest of all, the truest well-wisher, knowledge itself; you are beyond the inner mind and beyond the outer senses of hearing and the rest, and you take away the workings of the three qualities of nature.
O Shiva — you are the thunderbolt that broke the mountain of Jalandhar's pride, the husband of Parvati, the place this world is born from, and the one who smashed the whole sacrifice of Daksha.
O Vishnu — devotion is what is dear to you; for your devotees you are like the wish-granting cow, filling every longing of their hearts, and you carry away their greatest, hardest and most frightening troubles — and that is why you are called Hari, the one who takes away.
O Shiva — you give comfort, joy and whatever gift is asked of you; you want nothing for yourself, you are free of every flaw and every fault, and you wander the lanes of Kashi, the forest of bliss.
These beautiful lines of the names and mantras of Hari and Shankar take away the sorrow born of liking and hating and all such pairs; they are a mine of joy, and they are always a stairway to the world of Vishnu and the world of Shiva — this Tulsidas says with a clean and truthful tongue.

He is the sun that makes the lotus of the Sun dynasty bloom; his beauty is that of millions of Kamadevs; he is the Garuda that swallows the snake of the age of Kali; in his powerful arms he holds a fierce bow and arrows; a quiver is tied at his back, and his strength has no limit.
His eyes are like the petals of a red lotus, he is the home of all grace, and the lovely glow of his dark body is like a rain cloud. He wears yellow silk the colour of gold fresh from the fire; he is a master of every weapon, worshipped by the perfected ones and by the gods; and from his navel the lotus was born.
He is the seat of all beauty; the whole universe is his own form; he is deeply wise and his qualities are full of mystery; his greatness has no measure; no one can ever defeat him and no one can reach the end of his play; he is very hard to know; he is the lord of heaven and of freedom, and the axe that cuts the root of the tree of this world of coming and going.
He set Ahalya, the wife of the sage Gautam, free from her curse; he is skilled at guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice and always takes the side of his devotees; and in King Janak's court he broke Shiva's bow and took away the pride and the greatness of Parashuram, who blazed with power and with anger.
To keep his father's word in honour he gave up without a second thought a kingdom that even the gods find hard to let go of; and taking with him his brother Lakshman and Janaki — though he is the unborn Supreme Being — he played the part of a man and destroyed Ravan and the other wicked demons, to keep the three worlds safe.
He made the Dandak forest holy with his sacred lotus feet; he destroyed Marich, who came as a false deer; he is the lion that kills the elephant drunk on its own huge strength, that is Bali; and he is the truest of friends, who ended every sorrow of Sugriv.
Taking with him the fearsome and mighty bears and monkeys, in battle he put fear into warriors as huge as mountains, like Kumbhakarna; he bound the ocean with a bridge; he freed the whole company of the gods from Ravan's prison; and he destroyed ten-headed Ravan with his twenty great arms, and his whole family with him.
To destroy the crowd of wicked demons, the enemies of the gods, who were a heavy load on the earth, he came down here — and nothing can be compared to his reason for coming. He is spotless, faultless, one without a second, truly beyond all qualities, and taking maya with him he puts on qualities; he is the Supreme Being in human form, the king of kings. It is this Shri Ram I remember.
Shesh, the Vedas, Saraswati, Shiva, Narad and Sanak and his brothers sing his qualities forever, yet they cannot reach the end of his play. That same Shri Ram, the Lord of Ayodhya, dear to Shiva, is always and forever the ship that carries this Tulsidas across the ocean of sorrow.

Shri Raghunath, the Lord of Janaki, is the sun that destroys the darkness of liking and hating. His body is young, he is the home of light, he is being, awareness and bliss, the mine at the root of all joy, the one who gives the world peace, and he is beautiful beyond words.
His lovely, blessed glow is like a fresh, dark, rain-heavy cloud; around his waist he wears beautiful yellow silk; and on his head shines a golden crown set with jewels, blazing like hundreds of suns.
Earrings hang in his ears, a tilak is drawn on his forehead, his eyebrows are beautiful beyond words, and his large eyes are like red lotuses. He looks with a sidelong glance; he takes away the sorrow of all three worlds; and he is the swan that floats on the lake of the heart of Shiva, the enemy of Kamadev.
His nose is very lovely, his cheeks are charming, his teeth shine like diamonds, his lips are red like the bimba fruit, his smile is sweet, his throat is like a conch and his chin is beautiful beyond compare. His words carry great weight; whatever he resolves comes true, and he ends the sorrows of the gods.
On his chest shines a soft forest-garland of flowers of many colours and fresh tulsi leaves, and over that garland a swarm of bees, drunk on its sweet smell, is flying and humming.
On his chest is the beautiful mark of Shrivatsa; armlets are on his upper arms, bangles on his wrists, and a lovely necklace shines at his neck; at his waist the little golden belt makes a sweet sound. On the throne, at his left, sits Janaki, shining like a soft golden creeper beside a dark tamal tree.
His arms reach down to his knees; in his left hand is the bow and in his right a single arrow; and before him the whole gathering of sages, the gods, the perfected ones, the great gandharvas, human beings, the nagas and many kings and emperors bow down.
He is without sin, undivided, all-knowing, the Lord of everyone, and he will surely give us all that is good; he is completely skilled in the art of wiping away the pain of those who come to him for shelter. To this Shri Ramchandra, with Lakshman beside him, I bow.
His two lotus feet are the home of joy and the dwelling place of Kamala (Lakshmi) — that is, Lakshmi is always busy serving those feet. They are beautiful beyond words with the forty-eight marks, the thunderbolt and all the rest, and they have made the clean heart of the great devotee Hanuman their finest temple — that is, these lotus feet live forever in Hanuman's heart. At the feet of that Shri Ram, who takes all sorrow away, this Tulsidas has taken shelter.

O Lord of Kosala! O Lord of the universe! You alone are the well-wisher of the world; you have spread out a great play of your endless qualities. Your utterly pure deeds are sung by the four Vedas, by Shesh, by Shukdev, by Shiva, by Sanak and his brothers, and by the sages who sit and think deeply.
You took the form of a fish and made the earth into a boat to carry your devotees across (at the time of the great flood); your greatness has no measure. You are complete with the share of every sacrifice; you crushed the demon Hiranyaksha with his terrifying body, and as the boar you lifted the earth up and saved it.
O Murari! You took the form of a huge and frightening turtle and, when the ocean was being churned, you held the Mandarachal mountain on your hard back as it was sinking into the depths; as the mountain turned there, it felt to you like the pleasure of a good scratch. From the churning of the ocean you brought out nectar, the wish-granting cow, Lakshmi and the moon, and with this you gave the gods great joy.
You took the form of Narasimha, the man-lion of matchless strength, and tore apart your enemy, the wicked demon Hiranyakashipu, who tormented human beings, sages, perfected ones, gods and nagas and trampled the brahmins and the bounds of dharma — and so you filled your great devotee Prahlad with delight.
You took the form of Vaman, a young brahmin student, and to outwit King Bali you first asked for only three steps of earth, but while measuring you covered the whole universe with those three steps. (As you measured) water came from the nail of your toe — the Ganga, which makes all three worlds holy. You sent Bali down to the underworld and gave that kingdom to Indra, and so you took away the unbearable grief of Aditi, the mother of the gods.
To tear apart the herd of elephants that were the proud warrior kings, Sahasrabahu and the rest, you became the lion, and to make the crop of the brahmins green again you became the rain cloud — in this way you came as Parashuram; and as Ram you cut ten-headed Ravan with his twenty great arms to pieces with your fierce arrows. To that king of kings, Shri Ramchandra, I bow.
To take away the heavy burden of the earth, though you are the Supreme Self, pure Brahma, you appeared for the sake of your devotees in human form — the moon that makes the night-lily of the Vrishni family open and bloom, the husband of Radha, and the fire that burns down the forest of Kansa and the other wicked families.
Seeing the whole earth in distress under strong hypocrisy and empty show, you cut through the net of sacrifices and all such rituals. To that God — pure understanding itself, solid knowledge, full of every divine quality, unborn and kind, the Buddha — I offer my praise.
The minds of all people are dirty with the sins this age of Kali brings. In the night of delusion, to destroy the thick darkness of the barbarous, you will rise like the sunrise as the Kalki avatar, born as a son in the house of a brahmin named Vishnuyash! O Lord, take away the heavy weight of Tulsidas's troubles.

I bow to Shri Ramchandra, who gives every good fortune, who is a treasure house of blessing in every way, who is the form of the whole universe and the Lord of the universe, who gives joy to all, who is the bee that drinks the nectar from the lotus of Shiva's heart, whose beauty holds the heart, and who is the crown jewel of all kings.
Lord Ram, You are the home of every happiness, a heap of goodness, the giver of the deepest peace. Your name gives a person everything, and it is holy beyond measure. You are pure, calm, utterly spotless, knowledge itself, the destroyer of anger and pride, and the dwelling place of compassion.
No one can defeat You. You wear no labels, You are beyond the mind and the senses, unseen, spread through everything, one alone, never changing, unborn, with no second like You. Though You are the Supreme Self, You take nature along with You and appear before us; You are our greatest well-wisher, the one who moves every heart, endless, and beyond all qualities. To that Shri Ramchandra I bow.
You hold up the earth. You are beautiful, the husband of Lakshmi, the one whose beauty humbles the pride of Kamdev, the very limit of loveliness, the most charming of all. You are so hard to reach and so hard to see; no reasoning can know You, and no one can find the far end of Your play. Yet by Your grace You take away this world of coming and going, You show Yourself easily to those who love You, and love and humility are enough to win You.
You bring truth into being, You live in truth, and whatever You resolve comes true. You are always strong, full of divine power, content in Yourself, the one who carries off the greatest suffering. Dharma (right living) is Your armour. In the knowledge of Brahman and of action no one is Your equal. The brahmins worship You, You are dear to brahmins and to those who love You, and You are the one who killed the demon Mur.
O Hari! You are eternal, free of all clinging, forever free, with no trace of pride, the one who carries away our sins, knowledge itself, solid being and awareness and bliss, and the root cause of everything. You protect all; You are the master even of Yama, who as death devours all; You stand unmoved at the centre, Your splendour hidden from sight, and You pour out Your grace on those who love You.
You are the one who has arrived, the one still seeking, and the goal itself. You are the word and the one who speaks it. You are the mantra, the one who repeats it, and the name that is repeated. You are the creation and You are the Creator. You are the final cause of all. From Your navel the lotus came. Your body is dark and lovely like a rain cloud. You are both the God with form and the God without form; this whole visible world is You, and the one who sees it is also You.
You fill everything like the sky, untouched by craving; You are Brahman, and the Lord of the gods who grant boons. Your name is Vaikunth, and the pure young Vaman who kept the vow of celibacy. The perfected sages and the crowds of gods praise You always; You break false piety apart and pull it out by the roots.
You are a mountain of perfect joy, the one who takes away poor judgment, ignorance, and the threefold sickness of the qualities sattva, rajas and tamas. This Tulsidas has come to Your shelter in word, in thought and in deed; and to drink up his ocean of fear of birth and death, You are the sage Agastya himself.

Lord Ram, You are known through all the world, the master of the whole universe, the universe itself in form, the keeper of the world's order, the one who rides on Garud. You are Brahman. You are the Lord of Brahma and the other gods who grant boons, and the Lord of speech. You are everywhere, spotless, mighty in strength, and the ruler of the state of moksha (final freedom).
Primal nature and the great principle; sound, touch, form, taste and smell; sattva, rajas and tamas; all the gods; sky, wind, fire, clear water and earth; intellect, mind and the ten senses; the five life breaths called prana, apana, samana, vyana and udana; the thinking mind, the soul, time, the atom, and the great power of consciousness — every bit of it is nothing but You.
O crown jewel of kings! Everything seen and unseen is You; with no division in You, You play through the whole universe. This entire world rests in a single fragment of You. Lord Shiva bows at Your two lotus feet, and from those same feet the holy Ganga came down. You are the conqueror of all.
O Lord, You are the beginning, the middle and the end. You are present in everything. O God, the wise who speak of Brahman see You woven through all things, as thread runs through cloth, as clay is in the pot, as the garland is truly there in what we took for a snake, as wood is in the wooden elephant, and as gold is in the bangle, the armlet and every ornament.
So You are deeply hidden, deep beyond measure, the breaker of pride, the knower of every secret, Yourself unseen, beyond the mind and the senses, the teacher of all. You are knowledge, the knower and the thing known. True knowledge is dear to You, You are a treasure house of great glory, and You carry us across this terrible ocean of birth and death.
Whatever You will comes true; You bring the dissolution of the world and the great dissolution at the end. No mind or intellect can imagine You. You rest on the bed of Shesh, the serpent. Your eyes are like lotus flowers, a lotus grew out of Your navel, Your body glows dark like a rain cloud, and You are beauty piled high, as lovely as ten million Kamdevs.
You are easy to reach for those who love You, and out of reach for the wicked. Great hardships come to those who worship You, to test them. You destroy every fault in Your devotees. You are hard to come by, no one can overpower You, and You take away our hardest sorrows. You are the one who stripped away the pride that Sanak and his brothers, the sons of Brahma, took in their higher and lower learning.
You are pleased with those who love You, and You pull out by the root the pain of this world of birth and death. Your name, Ram, is the fire that burns sin as fire burns cotton. You are the sun that ends the night of restless craving. You hold up the earth, You take away the fear of everyone who comes to You, and You are the home of compassion.
Crowds of gods bow at Your two feet. On Your chest You wear a garland of mandar flowers. O Ram, enemy of Ravan! I, Tulsidas, always restless with grief, have come to Your shelter. My Lord, save me.

Lord Ram, You take away the sorrow of the saints; when the great dissolution comes, the whole universe rests in You; and You are the joy of Lord Shiva. You are the home of pure understanding, solid being and awareness and bliss, the one who makes good people's joy grow, and the enemy of the demon Khar.
Lord Ram, You are the home of good character and an even mind, the destroyer of the unevenness that comes from seeing others as separate, the beloved of Lakshmi and the enemy of Ravan. You carry arrows, a bow and a spear; a sword and a beautiful shield are in Your hands; armour covers Your body, and a quiver is strapped at Your handsome waist.
Whatever You will comes true; You give every blessing; You wish good to all; You are full of every divine quality, of knowledge and of the deeper knowing. Your name, Ram, is like the sun with its fierce rays, rising to end the night of this dreadful world that is packed with the thick darkness of ignorance.
Your splendour is sharp and blazing. You put an end to the fresh, fierce burnings this world keeps bringing. Though You wear the body of a king, Your true form is made of tapasya (self-discipline). You are beyond all ignorance, and You live as an ascetic. To churn the ocean of pride, arrogance, lust, envy, hungry wanting and delusion, You are Mount Mandar itself; and You weigh all things with deep thought.
The Vedas sing of You. You are the Lord of the gods who grant boons, the dwarf Vaman, free of attachment, spotless, the master of speech and the Lord of Vaikunth. You destroy lust, anger and greed, You make forgiveness grow, You are peace itself, and You ride on Garud, the king of birds.
You are utterly holy, and You are the fire that in a moment burns a whole thicket of heaped up sins down to its roots, as if it were dry munja grass. You are the ornament of the universe, the enemy of the demon Dushan, the Lord of the world, the husband of the earth, the crown of the Vedas, and the one who feeds and keeps the whole universe. Victory to You!
You are spotless, always the same, without parts and yet holding every part, and You end the restlessness of souls scorched by the heat of this age of Kali; You are joy piled high. You sleep on Shesh, the serpent, and Your eyes are like lotuses in full bloom. In visible form You live in the ocean of milk, and unseen You live in every being.
Those two feet of Yours, that bring such happiness to the perfected sages, to poets and to the learned, are far out of reach of people with evil hearts — those holy feet from which the Ganga came with her most sacred water, feet that wash away sins at a single sight of them.
You are eternal; You are wholly free of maya (the world's illusion); You are rich in divine qualities and untouched by the three qualities of nature; You are joy itself; You are the Lord who holds all six kinds of greatness; You make the laws and You rule over all. You feed and protect the whole universe, You are the first cause of the world, and You take away the fear of Tulsidas, who has come to Your shelter.

Lord Ram, You destroy the demons, You are an ocean of mercy, You clear away pretence, You burn evil deeds to ashes and You take away pride. You destroy wickedness, You are self-control itself, the greatest of all who have mastered their senses, You carry off whole heaps of sorrow, and You break the hard, ugly cravings in us.
You wear many ornaments and shine like the sun; You hold the six divine qualities, beginning with majesty; You set us free from this world; You give the gift of fearlessness; and You are the greatest Lord of all creation. You are beyond anything the mind or the intellect can feel or think. Lord Shiva bows to You, You do good to Shiva's devotees, You lifted the earth out of danger, and You held up the mountain Govardhan.
O giver of boons, Your body is dark as a rain cloud! You are the master of speech, the soul of the universe, free of all craving, and You move forever through the halls of Vaikunth. You fill all space like the sky; everyone bows to You; You took the form of the dwarf Vaman; nothing is beyond Your power; You know Brahman and You are Brahman; and You take our worries away.
You are beautiful by Your very nature, with a lovely face and a pure heart. You are always good, always spotless, You know everything, and You act freely, bound by no one. You do everything, You feed and keep everyone, You win over all, You wish good to all, whatever You will comes true, and at the end of an age it is You who bring the dissolution.
You are eternal, free of delusion, beyond all qualities, without a stain, joy that rests in itself; You are freedom itself and the giver of freedom. You are perfect bliss, unmoving, without limit, moksha (final release) in person, wearing no labels, holding on to nothing, and the maker of all.
You are the root of every great blessing, the home of joy and glory, the one who killed the foolish demon Madhu; You give honour to others and keep none for Yourself. You destroy Kamdev, You have no arrogance, maya cannot touch You, You are the husband of the beautiful goddess Lakshmi, and You hold a lotus in Your hand.
Your eyes are like lotus flowers. You are the storehouse of all sixty-four arts, the one who carries the bow, the Lord of Kosal, and a heap of blessing. You are the lion that kills the many maddened elephants that are the demons, and You live in the holy forest of Your devotees' hearts.
You are without sin, without a second, without fault, unseen, unborn, without limit, never changing, an ocean of joy. You never move, yet You do not live in one place only; You are everywhere, complete in every way, free of sickness, that is, untouched by the distortions of maya, and without beginning. And You are the elder brother of Lakshman, who killed Meghnad.
This Tulsidas is worn down by the sorrows of the world, caught in trouble, full of grief and badly frightened. O protector of all who come to You! O home of the highest mercy! O Ram, Lord of the earth! Save this ill-mannered servant of Yours.

O husband of Rama! Give me satsang, the company of the good, for it is the surest way to reach You, it ends the coming and going of this world, and it takes away the grief of everyone who runs to You for shelter. O Murari! Those who stay always at Your tender feet and keep to their love for You — every doubt born of ignorance is destroyed in them.
Demons and gods, serpents and human beings, yakshas, gandharvas, birds, night-wandering rakshasas, perfected sages and every other kind of creature — all of them, through the company of the saints who love You, reach that eternal highest place of Yours, beyond wealth, duty and desire, which no other practice can win, and which comes only when You are pleased.
Vritrasur, Bali, Banasur, Prahlad, Maya the demon builder, the hunter who became Valmiki, Gajendra the elephant, Jatayu the vulture, and Ajamil the brahmin who had fallen away from a brahmin's duties, and outcastes and foreigners too — all of them washed away every sin with the water from the saints' feet and came into a share of the highest good.
(And what are these holy people like?) Every desire has left their hearts, so they are calm; they long for no thing and no situation, so they depend on nothing; they cling to nothing, they wear no labels, they have gone past the three qualities of nature; among those who know the Vedas, the word that is Brahman, they stand first, and they know Brahman itself. They are skilled at finishing the work this human body was given for; they look on everyone with the same eye; they know their own true self; they have no thought of mine and yours, no sense of division; they see everything as belonging to their own Ram; and, O bearer of the discus, they have turned away from the world's pleasures and love You, the Supreme Self, and no one else.
Their hearts ache always to do good to the world; they have thrown away arrogance and anger, and they have earned a great wealth of merit. Wherever such saints live, Lord Hari, who dwells in the ocean of milk, comes running there of His own accord, bringing Brahma and Shiva along with Him.
(And what is this company of the good?) The Vedas are the ocean of milk, careful thought upon them is Mount Mandar, and all the crowds of sages are the ones who churn. From that churning came the nectar, the very essence, which is satsang. This truth is told by Lord Krishna Himself, the husband of Rukmini.
The true counsel of the saints destroys grief, doubt, fear, giddy excitement, ignorance and the whole crowd of cravings, just as the arrows of Raghunath destroy the massed armies of the demons with great skill and terrible speed.
Lord Ram, wherever my own karma may give me birth, through whatever kind of body I may wander, bearing one trouble after another, let me have Your love and the company of Your saints there, always. O Ram, let this alone be my one support.
For the three fierce pains this world brings — those from other beings, those from our own body, and those sent by fate — devotion to You is the only medicine, and Your devotees, who see only You in everything that moves and everything that does not, are the only doctors. In truth there is not the smallest difference between a saint and God — that at least is what Tulsidas, dull-witted as he is, keeps saying.

O beloved of Lakshmi! I am drowning in this ocean of the world; give me the support of Your lotus hand. For You are the one who takes away sorrow and destroys the deepest griefs. O destroyer of Dushan! You are Rahu, who swallows the moon of ignorance, and the lion that crushes the maddened elephants of pride and lust.
In the little universe that is this body, our rushing after things is the fort of Lanka, and the mind, like Maya the demon builder, has built it. The many sheaths in it (the body has five: of food, of breath, of mind, of understanding and of bliss) are its beautiful palaces, and the three qualities, sattva and the rest, are its generals.
The pride we take in the body is a sea around it, terrifying, bottomless, endless, impossible to cross, filled with crocodiles of liking and hating and wanting, while waves of attachment and scheming rise on it.
In this Lanka, delusion is Ravan, ego is his brother Kumbhakaran, and lust, which destroys all peace, is Meghnad.
Here greed is Atikaya, envy is the wicked Mahodar, anger is the great sinner Devantak, hatred is Durmukh, pretence is Khar, deceit is Akampan, arrogance is Manujad and conceit is the demon Shulapani; this whole crowd of demons (the wicked royal family and its commanders) is fiercely strong and very hard to beat. And along with these six demons, delusion and the rest, there are she-demons too, which are the senses.
My Lord, the soul that serves Your lotus feet is Vibhishan, living in that forest full of wicked ones, eaten up with worry. The ten guardians of the directions and Indra, who are the vows and disciplines of a good life, have fallen under this Ravan's rule and live in terror.
So, just as You came into the house of King Dasharath and Kausalya to lift the burden of the earth, O beloved of Janaki, come now into the house of Dasharath who is wisdom, through Kausalya who is pure devotion, and destroy these demons of delusion. And just as, seeing Your devotees' pain, You went away to the forest then at Your father's command, come now into the forest of my heart.
With all the practices that lead to moksha as Your many bears and monkeys, and with wisdom as Sugriv, build a bridge across this ocean of the world. Then strong detachment, mighty Hanuman the son of the wind, will burn the forest and the palaces of sense pleasure to ashes like fire.
And then, O pure solid knowledge! O Ram, who takes away the sorrow of the whole world! For the sake of this servant, this poor soul, destroy the wicked demon of delusion along with his whole family, and live forever in the lotus of Tulsidas's heart with Your younger brother Lakshman and with Janaki at Your side.

Lord Ram, You lift up the helpless, You are the finest of the line of Raghu, the home of compassion, the one who ends our burning grief and carries off whole heaps of sin. You never change, You are the deeper knowing itself, mercy given a body, the crown jewel of kings, the joy of the gods, and the enemy of the demon named Khar.
O Murari, this world is a forest, deep and full of terror. The trees in it are our actions, crowded thick together; creepers of craving twist around them; and sharp thorns of restlessness lie scattered everywhere. That is what it is: a dreadful forest of trees packed close.
In this forest, the many turnings of our thoughts are the flesh-eating birds, the hawks, owls, crows, herons and vultures. Every one of them is cruel and clever at tricks. The moment they see an opening, they wound the hearts of the travellers, the souls passing through.
In this forest of the world, anger is a maddened elephant, lust is a lion, arrogance is a wolf and pride is a bear, and not one of them knows any pity. Besides these there is the savage buffalo of envy, the boar of greed, the jackal of trickery and the cat of pretence.
Here too are the fierce monkeys of deceit and the tigers of false piety, forever tormenting the deer that are the saints and making havoc. O keeper of the world! With this sorrow in my heart I have come to Your shelter. My Lord, save me, save me.
In this forest of the world (even if you escape these creatures, more trouble waits ahead) stands the huge mountain of ego, which no one can climb over easily. In that mountain is a cave of great delusion, and inside it the darkness is thick. Here the thinking mind is a ghoul, the mind is a man-eating demon, diseases are the ghosts and spirits, and the poison of the scorpions of pleasure and luxury has spread everywhere.
Here the longing for sense pleasure is the flies and the mosquitoes, wicked people are the shrilling crickets, and, my Master, sight, taste, smell, sound and touch are the snakes. My Lord, Your hard maya has dragged this fool of a man here and thrown him down. O rider of Garud, I am blind; I have no eye of wisdom at all.
Through this forest of the world runs the river of birth and death, which is our craving, terrible and bottomless, brimming with the water of sin, hard even to look at and far harder to cross, for it has no far shore. In it are six crocodiles: lust, anger, greed, delusion, arrogance and envy; and it is crowded with the alligators of the senses and with whirlpools. Its two banks are our good deeds and our bad ones, and a fierce current of sorrow runs between them.
O ornament of the house of Raghu! This whole gang of low creatures has me in its grip, and Your servant Tulsi lives always in the hold of worry. I am frightened by this cruel age of Kali; in Your mercy, save me.

I bow to Nar and Narayan, who are the home of compassion, absorbed in deep meditation, and the source of all true knowing. They do good to the whole world, their hearts are full of mercy, they stay given to tapasya, and they pour out their grace on every devotee who comes to them for shelter.
Their bodies glow like a garland of fresh blue lotuses. Their beauty is that of ten million Kamdevs, and their light is that of countless suns. Their lovely eyes are like lotuses newly opened, their faces are beautiful as the moon, and their soft smile is like the moon's own rays.
They are the storehouse of all beauty, the dwelling place of every divine quality, and though Brahma, the Vedas, the learned and Lord Shiva all serve them, they carry no pride at all. From their red lotus feet came the Mandakini, the Ganga, like flowing nectar, and the sages, like bees, drink of it forever.
They crushed the arrogance of the fearsome Kamdev, whom Indra had sent against them; they hold no anger, they are pure understanding itself, and they keep the vow of celibacy. By their own power, with no age actually ending, they played out the whole scene of the world's dissolution, just to show it to the sage Markandeya.
They sit forever in Badrikashram, among its holy woods and mountains and rivers, seated in the lotus posture, always the same, never stirring. To see them, and nothing compares with that sight, brings joy and blessing even to the perfected sages, to the greatest of yogis and to the gods.
O keeper of the world! There on the road to Your Badrikashram stands a mountain called Manbhang, the heart-breaker (people who see it hesitate to go further), and here in my heart pride is my Manbhang, breaking the eagerness I need for my practice; there stands the mountain called Chittabhang, the mind-breaker, and here arrogance does exactly the work of Chittabhang; there the mountains are hard to climb, and here lust and greed and the rest are my hard mountains. (There the wild beasts and the like are the great dangers, and) here liking, hating, envy and many more are the great dangers, and every one of them is pitiless and crooked in what it does.
Here a lovely woman's sidelong glance is the dreadful edge of a knife, and the poison of desire is the sharp edge of a sword, and it wounds the minds of even the steadiest and most serious men; so what are weak people like me worth counting for?
My Lord, the road to the sight of You is hard enough to begin with; and on top of that I have fallen in with wicked, low company, and I do not even have the walking stick of detachment in my hand to lean on. This servant of Yours is desperate to see You, and he suffers, caught fast in a snare. My Lord, take away Your servant's pain and save him, save him.
Poor Tulsidas has no food packed for the road either, no dharma to carry him along the way; I am worn out and miserable, and delusion has destroyed even my good sense. So, O bearer of the discus, You who are splendour and strength and happiness heaped high, do not wait any longer; give me the support of Your lotus hand.

O Bindumadhav! You are the cloud that rains down every happiness, the one who makes Kashi, the forest of bliss, holy, the one who takes away the troubles born of attachment, hatred and all such pairs of opposites. At your lotus feet Brahma, Shiva, Sanak and Sanandan and the other sages, Shukdev, Shesh and many more live always, like bees.
Your dark form is like a flawless blue sapphire, your beauty is that of a billion Kamadevs, and you wear yellow silk that shines on you like lightning in a dark cloud. Your eyes are like red lotuses, your gaze is lovely, you give joy to your devotees, and by your very nature you stay soaked in compassion.
You are the lion that kills the elephant of death, the fire that burns down the forest of demons, and the sun that destroys the night of delusion. In your four arms you hold the conch, the discus, the mace and the lotus. The white conch in your hand shines like a royal swan sitting on a lotus.
A crown on your head, rings in your ears, a tilak mark on your forehead, black curls like a swarm of bees, arched eyebrows, beautiful teeth, lips and nose. Your lovely cheeks and your neck shaped like a conch are the very limit of all happiness. O Hari! Your sweet smile is like moonlight and like the white jasmine flower.
On your chest the great forest-garland with its fresh new blossoms and the beautiful mark of Shrivatsa are shining. You give great honour to the brahmins; you are without anger, unborn, of measureless strength, of vast glory, and without end. Blessed are you, blessed are you.
You wear a necklace on your chest, gold bands on your arms, jewelled bangles on your wrists, and a belt of gems at your waist. On both your feet are anklets that ring as sweetly as swans. Every limb of yours is beautiful, and your whole form is made of beauty.
Shri Lakshmi, daughter of the ocean, who holds all good fortune and is the beauty of all three worlds, sits at your right side. You live in a beautiful temple beside the Ganga; the people who see you with their own eyes are blessed indeed.
You are the home of every blessing, the one who destroys the hardest doubts, who burns the forest of sin to ashes and takes away all suffering. You hold up the whole universe, you wish the universe well, you cannot be defeated, you are beyond the mind and the senses, you are goodness itself, and you create, keep and dissolve the world.
You are the treasure-house of knowledge, of true understanding, of detachment and of majesty; you give even the great powers like anima, so freely do you give. The serpent of this world is swallowing me, Tulsidas, and I am terrified. So, O Ram, who ride Garuda, the destroyer of serpents, be kind and save me.

This is the one great fruit of having this body, and all its glory: that the eyes should drink their fill of the beauty of Shri Bindumadhav, from his feet to the crown of his head.
His spotless, youthful body, sixteen years old, strong and beautiful and dark, has beauty without any limit. It seems as if the blue lotus, the dark rain cloud, the tamal tree and the sapphire all got their beauty from this body of his.
His soft feet carry beautiful holy marks, the thunderbolt, the goad and the rest, and his toes and nails are like something never seen before, as if a cluster of jewelled leaves had sprung out of red and blue lotuses.
The golden anklets set with gems steal the mind away and give joy to his devotees, as if Lord Vishnu had taken many forms and built himself a beautiful temple in Shiva's heart and come to live there.
The sweet sound of the belt at his waist is beyond compare; it cannot be described. (Still, this much can be said.) It is as if bees were humming their lovely song among the buds of a golden lotus.
On his broad chest the print of sage Bhrigu's foot is marked, and it shows how soft that chest of yours is. The bangles and the many other ornaments are so lovely, it is as if Brahma had put his whole heart into it and made them with his own hands.
In the middle of a necklace of great pearls a setting of jewels shines so beautifully that it cannot be described. (But to help you picture it, it is said) that it is like the nine planets making themselves a seat in the middle of a circle of stars on a dark cloud. (The meaning is this: the Lord's body is the dark cloud, the necklace of pearls is the circle of stars, and the coloured gems strung here and there in it are the seats of the nine planets.)
His long arms, round and smooth as a serpent's body, are made beautiful by the lotus, the conch, the discus and the mace; his neck is the limit of beauty, and the endless loveliness of his face, with its chin and its lips, spreads over everything.
Looking at his teeth, diamonds, jasmine buds and the flash of lightning all hang their heads in shame. His nose, his eyes, his cheeks, the rings in his beautiful ears and his eyebrows are all very dear to me.
On his head are curls of hair, and over them he wears a crown; on his forehead the tilak mark shines with great beauty. Let me try to explain it: it is as if two small streaks of lightning had given up their restlessness and come to live in the circle of the moon.
On his body he wears pure yellow silk beyond all compare, and my heart cannot hold anything to compare it with. (Even so one imagines) that it is like a cloth of gold shining on the peak of a blue mountain studded with many gems.
At his right side Lakshmi sits with love. She looks so beautiful there, it is as if a golden vine wrapped in a blue cloth had come and sat beside a tamal tree.
If hundreds of Saraswatis, and Sheshnag, and all the Vedas together tried to describe this beauty, they still could not reach the end of it. Then how can this slow-witted Tulsidas, tangled in attachment and hatred and all such pairs, ever sing this beauty and describe it?

O my mind! The highest fruit of having this body is only this: leave your restless ways for a moment, and quietly, with love, look at the beautiful form of Shri Bindumadhav, lovely in every limb from his feet to the crown of his head.
His soft feet are like red lotuses that have just opened, and the light of his toenails takes away the darkness of ignorance in the heart. On those feet are the beautiful lines of the thunderbolt, the flag, the barley grain and the lotus. And the mark of the goad there brings the elephant of the mind under control.
On his feet are golden anklets set with gems, and at his waist the belt is ringing sweetly. On his belly are three folds, and his navel is deep like a pool, and from it wise ones like Brahma were born.
On his chest is the forest-garland, and in the middle of it a jewelled setting shines with great beauty; and the print of Bhrigu's foot simply pulls the heart away. The colour of his body is like a garland of blue lotus flowers, and on it the yellow silk seems to rain down beauty.
On his hands are lovely bangles and armbands, and the ring on his finger gives a joy all its own. In his four great arms, long as an elephant's trunk, he holds the conch, the discus, the mace and the lotus.
His neck, shaped like a conch, is the limit of beauty. Beautiful chin, teeth, red lips and a fine straight nose; eyes like fresh lotuses, a face like the full moon, and a soft smile that gives joy to his devotees.
His lovely cheeks, the rings in his ears, the crown on his head and the beautiful tilak on his forehead are all shining. His arched eyebrows are beautiful, his gaze is charming, and even a row of bees feels ashamed when it sees his black hair.
Shri Lakshmi, daughter of the ocean, the mine of beauty, goodness and every virtue, sits at his right side and serves his feet; and Shiva, Brahma, the sages, human beings, demons and gods all long for one kind look from her.
The fear of this world can leave Tulsidas only when his mind gets caught in this beautiful form; if not, he will go on wandering for millions of births, uselessly, wretched and stained and without any joy.

I bow to Shri Raghunath, the treasure of compassion, so that my habit of seeing difference in this world may fall away from me.
Shri Ram opens the lily of the Raghu line the way the moon does. Brahma and Shiva serve his lotus feet.
He lives in the lotus-heart of his devotees the way a bee lives in a flower. The beauty of his body is that of countless Kamadevs.
He is the sun that destroys the thick, stubborn darkness of delusion, and the fire that burns to ashes the dense forest of ignorance.
He is the generous sage Agastya who drinks up the ocean of pride, the one who gives joy to the gods and who (by crushing the demons) lifts the burden off the earth.
He is Garuda who eats up the snakes of attachment and hatred, the lion who kills the elephant of lust, and the one who killed the demon named Mur.
His lotus feet are the ship that carries us across the ocean of this world; and this Ram, the beloved of Janaki, rains down joy on us.
He plays forever like a swan in the pool of Hanuman's love, and for those devotees who ask for nothing he is like the wish-granting cow, kind beyond measure.
Tulsidas says only this: Shri Ramchandra, the crown jewel of the three worlds, the very forest of all good qualities, is the one and only home of peace.

O my tongue! Keep delighting in Ram, Ram; keep repeating Ram, Ram; keep saying the name of Ram over and over. And O my mind! You too become the papiha bird, and hold out stubbornly for that ever-fresh cloud, the love of Ram's name.
The papiha does not hope for even a drop of water from a well, a river, a pond, or even from the sea; it stays thirsty for one loving raindrop from the Swati star alone. In the same way, do not hope for any other practice or for the rewards they bring; love only that one drop of nectar, the love of Shri Ram's name.
The cloud it loves thunders at the papiha, scolds it, pours hailstones on it, hurls lightning at it, testing it in the hardest ways there are, weighing its undivided love to the very end. And when the cloud finds out that the more it tests the bird, the more that bird's love grows, (then the bird gets its drop of Swati rain).
In the same way, however many troubles come to test you and try to shake you (by God's own grace), you should take shelter in the name of Ram alone, with a heart that turns nowhere else; fix your mind on the name of Ram, become a lover of the name of Ram. All the devotees who have lived under the shelter of that name, all who live under it now, and all who will live under it later, are the ones who should be counted the most fortunate in the three worlds.
This one-pointed path, of loving Ram's name and nothing else, is very hard. If you do set out on it, then do not keep stopping every moment to rest in the shade of the world's pleasures. O Tulsidas! Your good will come only from keeping up, from your own side, an honest and open-hearted love for Shri Ram's name.

You madman! Say Ram, say Ram, say Ram. To get across this terrifying ocean of the world, the name of Ram is your own boat. That is, once a person sits in this boat of Ram's name he can cross over whenever he wishes, because it lies in his own hands.
With the strength of this one practice alone, win every power and every attainment, because the disease of this Kali age has swallowed up practices like yoga, self-control and deep meditation.
Good or bad, crooked or straight, in the end every one of us will have to turn to this one name of Ram.
This world is completely false, like a garden that our confusion makes us see blooming and fruiting in the empty sky. These worldly things appear and vanish from one moment to the next, like palaces of smoke; do not look at them and be fooled.
Whoever leaves the name of Ram and puts his trust in something else, O Tulsidas, is like that fool who leaves the food already served in front of him and goes from house to house like a dog, begging for one mouthful here and one mouthful there.

O soul! Always repeat the name of Shri Ram with a love that turns nowhere else. In this Kali age, nothing at all can be gained from renunciation, yoga, yajna (sacrifice), penance or charity, apart from the name of Ram.
The scriptures lay out what we should do and what we should not do. In my view, remembering the name of Shri Ram is the king of everything we should do, and forgetting the name of Shri Ram is the very worst of everything we should not do.
The name of Ram is a great jewel, and this net of the world is a snake. Just as a snake, once its jewel is taken away, grows helpless and lies as good as dead, so this painful net of the world falls apart on its own once you take up the jewel of Ram's name.
Listen! This name of Ram is the wish-granting tree. It gives all four fruits: wealth, dharma (right living), desires fulfilled, and moksha (freedom for the soul). The Vedas, the Puranas, the learned, and even Lord Shiva himself say so.
The name of Shri Ram is the heart of both love and the highest gain, that is, of both devotion and freedom; and for this Tulsidas that name of Ram is the very support of his life.

O soul! Until your tongue repeats the name of Ram, you may go wherever you like, and you will still keep burning in the three kinds of suffering.
Even standing on the bank of the Ganga you will go thirsty and be miserable without water; even under the wish-granting tree, poverty will keep tormenting you.
Awake, asleep, or in your dreams, you will find no happiness anywhere; in this world, birth after birth and age after age, all you will do is weep.
The more other ways you try to get free (with your back turned on Ram's name), the more tightly you will be tied up; even food of pure nectar will turn to poison for you.
O Tulsi! For a helpless one like you, in all three worlds and in all three ages, the name of Shri Ram is the only support, just as water is for a fish.

O soul! Remember with love the name of Shri Ram, the king of kings. His name is the food for the road for travellers who set out with nothing to eat, and it is the helper of anyone who has no helper.
This name of Ram is fortune for the unlucky and merit for those with no merit. (Even the unlucky and the unworthy, if they repeat Ram's name, become the most fortunate of all and full of every good quality.) It is the one buyer who gives the poor their worth, and the kind giver to the helpless.
This name of Ram is high birth for those born low (even an outcaste who repeats Ram's name is counted the highest of all), and hands and feet for the crippled and eyes for the blind (those who repeat Ram's name walk over the road of this world with ease). The Vedas themselves stand witness to this truth.
This name of Ram is mother and father to the hungry and the one support of those who have no support. It is the bridge for crossing the ocean of this world, and the chief means of reaching God, in whom every happiness is contained.
Who else lifts up the fallen the way the name of Ram does? By remembering it, even a barren, salty patch of ground like Tulsi turned into beautiful, fertile soil, rich with the crop of love and devotion.

O my mind! If you do as I say, and love the name of Shri Ram as naturally as you breathe, then everything will go well for you in every way.
The power of Ram's name is like a fire that drives away the shivering cold. This Kali age, which unsettles a person's mind, will run away at once in fear of Ram's name, along with all its helpers, lust and anger and the rest.
By the power of Ram's name, detachment, yoga, the repeating of the name, and penance will all wake up on their own; and then even a hostile fate will not be able to write the fruit of bad deeds on your forehead, that is, all your karmas will wear away to nothing.
If you soak the sweet ball of Ram's name in the nectar of love and then eat it, you will find the deepest contentment for all time, and you will never again have to wander from door to door looking for happiness.
The name of Ram is the wish-granting tree, so, O Tulsidas, whatever you ask of it, for this world or for the next, you will be given it all, and nothing will be left wanting.

Look at you, holding yourself back even from the service of such a Master! You have no sense of your own, and you pay no attention to what anyone else tells you either. You are of no use at all; you are a stone lying in the road.
The Lord Shri Ram, whom even the minds of sages cannot reach, is as easy for his devotees to reach as their own mother and father. He is an ocean of kindness, a friend by his very nature, and he loves us of his own accord.
It is well known in the world and in the Vedas that there is no one greater than Shri Raghunath, and that he is always there, everywhere, with every one of us.
(Love Shri Ram with a true heart, because) that Master knows everything; a servant's cheating cannot stay hidden from him. In that court only love is recognised, and that is the rule of his court.
In his service the body is not put to even the smallest trouble; that Master takes the love and the service of the heart alone as enough. The moment you remember him with love he feels shy, and he begins to look for what his servant would like. That is, even after giving his devotees whatever they wish for, he is still embarrassed, thinking that he has given nothing at all.
Whoever he is pleased with, he gives himself into that person's hands; and whoever he is angry with, he sends to his own highest home, setting him free from the chains of the body. His name is like the wish-granting tree, on which every kind of fruit grows.
Here is a man who would not fetch a single bad coin if he were sold, and who is of no use to anyone if he is kept. Even this Tulsidas he has made rich and glad. What can anyone say about such a king of kings, Shri Ram?

Shri Ram has done me good purely out of his own goodness. (What hope was there of any good coming out of what I do?) For I am the one who does wrong to his Master; but my Master Shri Ram is the one who does good to his servant.
Who is greater than Shri Ram, and who is smaller than I am? Who is as true as he is, and who is as false as I am?
The world says that I, Tulsidas, am Ram's slave, and I let myself be called that. (Though I am not really Ram's servant, I accept the title.) This is a very great offence of mine; and even so, Shri Ram's heart has not turned away from me in the least.
O Tulsi! A blade of grass is a lowly thing, yet it rises to the very top of the water and floats there; and still the water does not drown it, because it takes the grass for something it watered and raised itself. (This is just how Lord Shri Ram thinks of me.)

You foolish soul, wake up, wake up! Look at this night that is the world! Know that your love for this body and for your home and family is as brief as lightning between clouds, which flashes for a moment and then hides away.
(And it is not only while you are awake.) Even while you sleep, in your dreams, you are suffering the pains of this world. Oh, in your confusion you are drowning in the water of a mirage, and a rope is biting you as if it were a snake.
The Vedas and the wise are calling out again and again; think it over in your own mind and understand that all the sorrows and faults of a dream really end only when you wake up.
O Tulsi! The three sufferings of this world end only when you wake up from the sleep of ignorance, and only then is a pure, natural love for the name of Shri Ram born in you, a love that asks for nothing in return.

It is Shri Ram's grace alone that wakes the wise souls who have taken shelter in his name out of the sleep of ignorance. So, by the power of Ram's name, leave your foolishness behind, wake up, and love Shri Hari. Think about what lasts and what does not, let go of lust, anger and every other flaw, and worship Shri Ramchandra, the ocean of blessing, the friend of the helpless, the generous one. This is what the Vedas command.
You have slept away a long time in the long, moonless night of delusion, and, lost in the dream of maya (the world's illusion), you have forgotten your own matchless true self. Look, morning has come now, and as the sun of wisdom rises, the thick darkness of craving, attachment, delusion and hatred is gone.
Seeing that morning had come, the thieves of pride and vanity began to run, and the crowds of demons, lust and anger and greed and restlessness, took fright on their own. The moment they saw the fierce splendour of Shri Raghunath, sin and torment were destroyed, and the three kinds of suffering were cooled by the water of love for Shri Ram.
Hearing this deep voice with their own ears, the brave and steady saints woke out of the sleep of delusion, and gladly took to themselves the beauty of detachment, contentment and all the rest. O Tulsidas! Seeing his devoted souls in distress, the merciful Shri Ramchandra tore the net of this world to pieces and began to give them the highest joy.

Bad or good, whatever I am, I am yours. I swear it by you; why would I lie to you? You know what is in every heart. I am not saying this to deceive you: with my deeds, my words and my heart I say, "I am yours." This stubborn hold I keep on being your slave is as tight as a knot of hemp soaked in water.
O Ram! I have no trust in anyone else, and I have no wish to worship Indra or Brahma or any other god, or any man or sage. Apart from you they are all friends for their own gain; serve them your whole life like an elephant, and somewhere at the end they toss you a scrap fit for a dog. Not one of them feels for the sorrow of the helpless the way you do.
O shining Lord, if what I say, "I am your slave," is a lie, then let this body of mine be given, right in front of you, the same unbearable punishment that a false snake-charmer gets in a gathering of snakes, a man who does not know the spell to control them; that is, let the snakes bite this fraud. And if I am proved true, a real slave of Ram, then, my Lord, let me be handed the token of truth before the elders. For this Tulsi is a chatak bird whose only hope is that one dark cloud, Ram.

I am Shri Ram's slave. People have started calling me "Rambola". The only work I do is that now and then I say Ram's name two or four times. And for that much, Ram keeps me well in food and clothes. That is how it is in this world; and for the world to come, the Vedas are calling out that by the power of Ram's name all will be well with me. That alone is why I stay happy always.
Once, my lifeless deeds had bound me in the hard irons of pride. It was such a terrible pain that it is unbearable even to hear about. In my misery I cried out, "O Lord of the suffering and the orphaned! O King of Kosal! O ocean of mercy! I am in great pain." (The moment he heard this,) Shri Ram saw me, helpless and burning in my sins, and at once set me free from the chains of my deeds.
The moment he asked me, "Who are you?" I said, "My Lord, I want to be your servant. I have nobody anywhere and nothing at all; I am lying here at your feet." At this Shri Ram, who gives joy to his devotees, the highest teacher, patted me on the back, took me by the arm, made me his own, and comforted me. Since that day I have always worn this Vaishnav dress of the Lord: the neck beads, the tilak mark, the rosary, the repeating of Ram's name, hurting no one, seeing no difference between people, humility and all the rest.
Seeing me become Ram's slave, people call me low; but this gives me no worry and no shame at all, because I have no marriage or match to arrange with anyone, and I have nothing to do with caste or clan. Whether Tulsi is made or ruined rests on nothing but Shri Ram being pleased or displeased with him. And I trust in your love, and that is why my heart is always full of joy.

Lord Ram! You are the life of Janaki, the breath of the universe, the well-wisher of the world, the master of the world, the lord of the house of Raghu, and your eyes are like lotus flowers. Your face is like the full moon of an autumn night, and giving joy is your very nature. Lakshmi lives in you always. Your body is beautiful by its own nature, beautiful beyond measure — its loveliness is like that of countless gods of love.
You are the world's father who gives it joy, its mother, its teacher, its well-wisher, its friend, and you are good to everyone. You are the friend of the helpless, and you never do harm to anyone. You take away trouble, you give shelter, you give without limit, you protect whoever comes to you, and you are full of mercy. Your name, Ram, makes even the fallen pure.
The whole world bows to you, all the gods serve you, and every Veda and scripture sings of your many virtues. Knowing all this, Tulsidas has become your slave. Now tell me — will you count him as an outsider, or will you write his name on the list of your poor slaves?

Lord Ram! There is no one else who takes pity on the helpless and gives them the highest joy. Whoever I tell my troubles to, I find that he is helpless himself. (What can someone give who has nothing of his own?)
There are plenty of masters — gods, human beings, sages, demons, serpents and the rest — but they last only as long as your glance does not turn even a little. The moment your look turns away, they let go of us too.
In all three worlds, in all three times, everywhere, this is what is known, and this is what the four Vedas say: at the beginning, in the middle and at the end, Ram, your greatness is always the same.
The beggar who once asked from you was never called a beggar again. (He received the highest, unending joy, and was satisfied forever, with nothing left to want.) Hearing the beautiful fame of this nature of yours, this servant has come to beg from you.
You have taken as your own even a stone (Ahalya), animals (the monkeys and bears), trees (the Yamalarjuna trees) and birds (Jatayu, Kakbhushundi). Son of King Dasharath, you have made lowly paupers into kings.
You make the poor rich beyond measure, and I am your poor slave. Merciful One! Just once, for this reason, say these words: "Tulsidas is mine."

Lord! You are the one who shows mercy to the helpless — and I am helpless. You give without limit — and I am a beggar. I am a well-known sinner — and you are the one who destroys whole heaps of sin.
You are the protector of those who have no one — and who has less of anyone than I do? No one is as miserable as I am, and no one takes away misery like you.
You are Brahman, I am a soul. You are the master, I am the servant. What more is there to say — you alone are my mother, my father, my teacher, my friend, my good in every way.
There are many ties between you and me; take whichever tie pleases you. But the real thing is this, Merciful One: let this Tulsidas somehow find shelter at your feet.

Lord! Who else should I hold out my hands to now? Who else is there who could end my begging forever? Who else gives whatever the heart wishes, and would destroy my sorrow and my poverty?
Shri Ram! You are the home of dharma, and more beautiful than the beauty of ten million gods of love. You are my master in every way, you know my mind through and through, and you are a great warrior at wielding the sword of giving.
In good times the drums beat at everyone's door for a day or two, but son of Dasharath, you give in such a way that you make the poor rich even in their worst days.
People who did you no service at all, who had not one good quality in them, poured out their sorrow before you, and you made every one of them rich — I have seen them walking about, blooming with joy.
Now know what is in the mind of the beggar Tulsidas (that he wants nothing else at all, only your love), and give him this gift: Shri Ramchandra, you are already the moon — just make me the chakor bird that lives by gazing at it.

Most merciful Lord of the Raghus! You are the friend of the helpless, an ocean of joy, a mine of mercy. Listen, Lord: my mind is burning with the three kinds of suffering of this world — or say it has caught the triple fever of lust, anger and greed — and that is why it raves like a madman.
Sometimes it practises yoga, and sometimes it is caught in wicked pleasures. Sometimes it stubbornly gives itself up to the pain of separation, and sometimes, held by delusion, it turns hostile in all sorts of ways — and then that same mind will suddenly be full of pity.
Sometimes it becomes poor, dull-witted, an utter pauper; sometimes it becomes a proud king. Sometimes it is a fool, sometimes a scholar. Sometimes it is a hypocrite, and sometimes a wise man devoted to dharma.
Lord! Sometimes the whole world looks to it like money, sometimes like enemies, sometimes like women — that is, it is caught now in greed, now in anger, now in lust. This terrible suffering, this delirium-fever of worldly life, can never be destroyed without God's mercy.
There are many medicines — self-control, chanting, penance, rules, dharma, vows and more — but the disease of worldly life in Tulsidas cannot be cured without love for the feet of Shri Ram.

The many kinds of filth of sin that come from delusion cling to me, and ten million remedies will not get them off. For many births this mind has been practising how to live in sin, and so this filth wraps itself around me more and more.
My eyes have been dirtied by looking at other men's wives, my mind has been dirtied by keeping company with the pleasures of the senses, my heart has been dirtied by craving, ego and pride, and my soul has been dirtied by giving up my own true nature, which is joy itself.
My ears have been dirtied by listening to gossip against others, and my speech by talking about other people's faults. It is only because I forgot the feet of my Lord Shri Ram that this load of filth follows me about in every way.
To wash this sin away the Vedas prescribe many remedies — vows, charity, knowledge, penance and more; but Tulsidas, without the water of love for Shri Ram's feet, this filth of sin cannot be destroyed root and all.
